text.p: Bangladesh's main opposition leader Begum Khaleda Zia has warned against what she called attempts to rehabilitate a "fallen autocrat" and called for resisting such conspiracies.

"A conspiracy is now on to rehabilitate a fallen autocrat. Such move will jeopardise the country's hard-earned democracy," Khaleda, chief of Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP), said in a statement published on Wednesday.
"I urge all freedom and democracy-loving people to resist the conspiracy," the former prime minister said.

Khaleda did not name former president Hossain Mohammed Ershad, deposed in an opposition-led popular revolt in December 1990, in her remarks, but it's well known that she refers to him as "fallen autocrat."

The BNP and Awami League of current Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, then both in opposition, jointly led the 1990 campaign, but became rivals after Khaleda won the 1991 elections to become the country's first woman prime minister and during her five-year tenure.
Now with Hasina in the saddle following last June's general election, Khaleda has asked her followers to launch a "vigorous movement" to topple her.
Ershad, in jail ever since he lost power, has meanwhile struggled to regain his freedom and has already made a strong comeback to politics.
The former president was sentenced by a special tribunal to 10 years in prison in June 1991 for possession of unlicensed firearms, but the High Court last year quashed the sentence.
Later he was charged in 16 more cases of corruption and misuse of power.
Ershad contested the last election from jail as chief of the opposition Jatiya party, and won five parliament seats.
His party lent support to Hasina's Awami League to form the government. Hasina has appointed the Jatiya's seceretary-general Anwar Hossain Manju as her communication minister.

Khaleda, leaving on Wednesday for Saudi Arabia for medical treatment, told her followers on Tuesday that Hasina was clearly in a "conspiratorial deal" with the Jatiya party to save her "corrupt and inefficient" government.
"But BNP will launch a relentless campaign soon to foil all evil designs."
